hook.from: Geography > Location, Terrain, Natural resources; Economy > Exports
hook.excerpt: Central Africa, south of Libya || broad, arid plains in center, desert in north, mountains in northwest, lowlands in south || Chad is the largest of Africa's 16 landlocked countries a wide variety of animals lived in modern-day Chad during the African Humid Period, including elephants, giraffes, hippos, and antelope; the last remnant of this "Green Sahara" exists in the Lakes of Ounianga in northern Chad, a series of 18 interconnected freshwater, saline, and hypersaline lakes Lake Chad, the most significant water body in the Sahel, is a remnant of a former inland sea, paleolake Mega-Chad; at its greatest extent, sometime before 5000 B.C., Lake Mega-Chad was the largest of four Saharan paleolakes that existed during the African Humid Period; it covered an area of about 400,000 sq km (150,000 sq mi), roughly the size of today's Caspian Sea || Resources: petroleum, uranium, natron, kaolin, fish (Lake Chad), gold, limestone, sand and gravel, salt || Exports: crude petroleum, gold, oil seeds, gum resins, cotton (2023)

physicalGeography.excerpt: broad, arid plains in center, desert in north, mountains in northwest, lowlands in south || Central Africa, south of Libya

climate.excerpt: tropical in south, desert in north || hot, dry, dusty harmattan winds occur in north; periodic droughts; locust plagues

economy.excerpt: oil-dependent economy challenged by market fluctuations, regional instability, refugee influx, and climate vulnerability; high levels of extreme poverty and food insecurity; recent growth driven by oil and agricultural recovery; debt-restructuring agreement under G20 Common Framework || Exports: crude petroleum, gold, oil seeds, gum resins, cotton (2023) || Industries: oil, cotton textiles, brewing, natron (sodium carbonate), soap, cigarettes, construction materials
